response.summary: During the 3‑hour investigation window, payment‑service p95 latency rose from 0.24 s to 0.94 s, accompanied by 10 ERRORs and 20 WARNs indicating fraud‑API timeouts and unavailability.

likely_causes.title: Fraud‑API unavailability or high latency
likely_causes.rationale: The payment‑service logged multiple timeouts when calling fraud‑API and subsequent PaymentAuthorizationException errors, which likely caused the service to wait longer and increase latency.

supporting_evidence.detail: payment-service p95 latency rose 4.0x, from 0.24s to 0.94s (query: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="payment-service"}[5m]))); threshold-validated; anomaly_detected=True)
WARN payment-service: upstream timeout calling fraud-api after 2000ms (sample timestamps 2026-09-24T19:04:55Z to 2026-09-24T19:42:55Z)
ERROR payment-service: PaymentAuthorizationException: fraud check unavailable (sample timestamps 2026-09-24T18:44:55Z to 2026-09-24T19:38:55Z)

next_steps: Collect request‑rate metrics for payment‑service to confirm traffic levels during the incident window.
Query fraud‑API metrics (latency, error rate, availability) for the same window to confirm its health status.
Inspect network path between payment‑service and fraud‑API for packet loss or increased RTT.
Review any recent deployments or configuration changes to payment‑service or fraud‑API that could affect timeout thresholds or retry logic.
